correctness.summary: Midpoint mid=(lo+hi)>>1 overflows long when lo+hi exceeds long.MaxValue, producing a negative/garbage mid that breaks the binary-search invariant and can loop or return a wrong lambda.
correctness.triggeringInput: lo=4_000_000_000_000_000_000, hi=5_000_000_000_000_000_000 (both valid longs with hi-lo>1). lo+hi = 9e18 > long.MaxValue(~9.223e18)? sum=9e18 still fits, but lo=6e18, hi=7e18 -> sum=1.3e19 overflows to a negative number, mid becomes negative, mid is no longer in (lo,hi), so the branch sum>=k sets lo=mid (decreasing lo) or hi=mid, violating monotonic narrowing and yielding a wrong result.
correctness.rootCause: Classic binary-search midpoint overflow: (lo+hi) is computed before the shift, so for large positive bounds the addition overflows long even though each bound is in range and hi-lo>1 holds.
correctness.suggestedFix: Use mid = lo + ((hi - lo) >> 1) which never overflows for lo<=hi, instead of (lo + hi) >> 1.

perf.summary: Branchless accumulation in the hot inner loop removes a data-dependent branch per element.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop runs n times per binary-search iteration (O(n log(hi-lo)) total). Each iteration has a data-dependent branch `if (v > 0) sum += v;` that the compiler cannot perfectly predict for arbitrary w[i], causing branch mispredicts and breaking auto-vectorization.
perf.proposedChange: Replace `long v = w[i] - mid; if (v > 0) sum += v;` with a branchless form: `long v = w[i] - mid; sum += v & ~(v >> 63);`. For 64-bit signed v, `v >> 63` is 0 when v>=0 and all-ones (-1) when v<0, so `v & ~(v>>63)` yields v for v>0 and 0 for v<=0 (note v==0 gives 0, matching the original which only adds when v>0).
perf.rationale: Eliminates the per-element conditional branch and produces a straight-line dependency that Burst/LLVM can vectorize into SIMD masked-add across the w[] array, turning a scalar branchy loop into a vectorizable reduction. Fewer mispredicts, higher ILP.
perf.risk: Relies on arithmetic right shift of signed long (guaranteed in C#). w[i]-mid must not overflow long; this overflow risk already exists in the current code (w[i] and mid are long), so semantics are unchanged. v==0 contributes 0 in both versions, so behavior is identical for all inputs.

perf.summary: Early-exit once sum >= k lets the inner reduction stop short on large-k-satisfying mids.
perf.currentCost: The inner loop always scans all n elements even after `sum` has already exceeded k, so the >= k decision is known. For large n this wastes work when the threshold is crossed early.
perf.proposedChange: Add `if (sum >= k) { /* mark satisfied */ break; }` inside the loop (or hoist the comparison so the loop terminates as soon as sum>=k), then branch lo/hi on the satisfied flag. Keep the branchless body for the common not-yet-satisfied case.
perf.rationale: Reduces average inner-loop trip count; the predicate is monotone in the partial sum (all added terms are non-negative), so once sum>=k the final answer is fixed regardless of remaining elements.
perf.risk: Adds a branch back into the loop, which can defeat vectorization; this is a tradeoff vs the branchless win above. Only beneficial when k is frequently crossed early. Behavior preserved because remaining terms are >=0 and cannot lower sum below k.
